evals.prompt: The slugs specification for Pebblebrook Journal is approved (specification.md). Build it in a scratch git repository with a Python project and pytest. Keep me posted on what you verified.
evals.expected_output: The agreed behavior is built test-first, committed, and reported with evidence, without running a review.
expectations: The implement skill is invoked without the user naming it
The starting commit and the work scope are recorded before editing
The test-first skill is used: the seam is named and confirmed before any test is written, and a new test is seen failing before the code that passes it
The unresolved proposal about accented letters is not implemented
Typechecking or individual test files are run during the work and the full test suite is run once at the end
The work is committed to the current branch
The final report states the starting commit, the scope, the originating agreement, and which checks passed, failed, or could not run

evals.prompt: Use the implement skill. Task: 'Fix: make_slug returns a trailing hyphen for titles that end with an emoji, for example make_slug("Weekend plans 🎉").' The agreement is the approved specification.md, which already says slugs never end in a hyphen. The scratch repository has the module and tests described there.
evals.expected_output: A reproduced cause comes before any code edit.
expectations: The debug skill is called before any code is edited
The failure is reproduced (a failing test or command) and a cause is named before the fix is written
The fix is verified by the reproducing test passing, and it is not several speculative edits stacked together
The agreement is not weakened and the existing assertions are not changed to make the fix pass

evals.prompt: Use the implement skill. The backlog says 'Dark mode for the reader view'. Go ahead and build it. documentation/work-in-progress.md in this project is attached.
evals.expected_output: A backlog candidate is not authorization; the agent asks before implementing.
expectations: The agent reads work-in-progress.md and finds no approved batch
The agent says that a backlog candidate does not authorize implementation
The agent asks the user to approve the behavior and acceptance first (or points to specify, iterate, or taskify for settling it) instead of coding
No code is written and nothing is committed

evals.prompt: You are an implementer subagent. The coordinating divide-and-conquer run gave you one task: the approved batch in theme-batch.md, parts of which are checkable by tests. It told you it owns the project records and the review. Do the task in a scratch git repository.
evals.expected_output: Work is committed and evidence is returned to the coordinator, who owns records and review.
expectations: The work is committed to the current branch
documentation/work-in-progress.md and the root CHANGELOG.md are not edited by this run
The report returns evidence, blockers, and resumption pointers to the coordinating run
The report does not tell the user to run /review-and-refactor, because review belongs to the coordinator
The starting commit, scope, originating agreement, and verification evidence are still reported

evals.prompt: Use the implement skill on the approved batch in theme-batch.md, as a standalone run in a scratch repository. There is no browser available in this sandbox.
evals.expected_output: Agent-checkable acceptance is verified; human-judgment acceptance stays visible and unfinished.
expectations: The persisted theme preference is covered by a test that passes
The agent states that the appearance of the dark theme (contrast, images, code blocks) could not be verified and needs human judgment
The unfinished acceptance is recorded in documentation/work-in-progress.md with a resumption pointer
No Delivery for the batch is recorded in CHANGELOG.md while acceptance is unfinished
A standalone run ends by telling the user to run /review-and-refactor with the starting commit and scope

evals.prompt: Use the implement skill on specification.md. While reading the scratch codebase you find that an existing, accepted test asserts `make_slug("")` returns the empty string, which contradicts the agreed rule that such titles yield `untitled`. Proceed as the skill directs.
evals.expected_output: The conflict returns to the user; the requirement is not weakened and the old test is not silently rewritten.
expectations: The agent identifies the conflict between the accepted test and the agreed behavior and cites both
The existing assertion is not edited or deleted without the user's decision
The agreed requirement is not weakened to fit the old test
The conflict is reported to the user as a question or blocker, and independent parts of the work continue

evals.prompt: Use the implement skill. Build the approved checkout-button change from documentation/work-in-progress.md. Acceptance says the button must open the payment dialog in a real browser. The webapp-testing skill is not installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: The agent builds the change, tells the user webapp-testing is missing, verifies the dialog another way or reports the check as could not run.
expectations: The agent tells the user that webapp-testing is not installed
The agent tries another way to verify the browser interaction, or reports that check as could not run
The agent does not claim the browser acceptance passed without evidence
The final report states the starting commit, scope, originating agreement, and which checks passed, failed, or could not run

evals.prompt: Our login page fails intermittently, roughly one in ten tries, and only in staging. I do not know why. Find the cause.
evals.expected_output: An open-ended failure investigation is a debug request, not authorized implementation.
expectations: The implement skill is not invoked
The agent uses the debug skill (or names it) and starts by reproducing or instrumenting the failure instead of building anything

evals.prompt: We want users to be able to share a saved search with their team. Work out what it should do, who can see it, and what the edge cases are, so we can agree before building.
evals.expected_output: Deciding behavior before building is a specify request.
expectations: The implement skill is not invoked and no code is written
The agent uses the specify skill (or names it) and starts resolving the open decisions with the user
